title: 己亥岁·其一
author: 曹松
intro: War has reached even the quiet lakes and rivers of the south, and ordinary people can no longer gather firewood in peace. Its last line — “one general’s glory, ten thousand dried bones” — is still the sharpest thing ever said in Chinese about the cost of war.
analysis: 己亥年是唐僖宗乾符六年（879年）。当时黄巢起义军转战南方，唐朝军队和起义军在长江、淮河一带反复交战，水乡也被卷进了战争。第一句说：江南水乡的山山水水都已经画进了作战地图，意思是到处都在打仗。第二句说：老百姓连上山砍柴、割草这种最普通的生活都过不下去了，还有什么办法快乐呢？后两句是全诗的重点：请你别再跟我谈什么立功封侯的事了，一个将军的功业，是用成千上万士兵的白骨换来的。“一”和“万”、“成”和“枯”形成强烈对比，这种写法叫“对比”，让读者一下子看清战争的代价。这一句后来成为人们批评战争、批评追求个人功名时最常引用的名句。
analysisEn: Jihai is the name of a year in the traditional sixty-year cycle; here it is 879. Huang Chao’s great rebellion was sweeping through southern China, and government troops and rebels fought back and forth across the rivers and lakes between the Yangtze and the Huai. The first line says the whole “land of marshes” — the quiet water country of the south — has been drawn onto the war maps: fighting is everywhere. The second asks how ordinary people can enjoy even the simplest life now, such as going out to cut firewood and grass. The second half is the heart of the poem. “Please don’t talk to me about winning glory and titles,” the poet says, because one general’s success is built on ten thousand withered bones. The contrasts — one against ten thousand, “success” against “withered” — are stark and simple, and they make the price of war impossible to ignore. That last line has been quoted ever since whenever people criticise war, or anyone who climbs to fame over other people’s lives.
background: Cao Song (c. 830–c. 903) was a poor scholar who failed the examinations for decades and is said to have finally passed the jinshi in 901, in his seventies. He wrote two poems titled “The Year Jihai”; this first one is by far the better known.
pronunciation: 一将 jiàng（将领，不读 jiāng）；乐樵苏 lè qiáo sū；凭君 píng jūn。
version: 采用通行版本。原作共两首，网站收第一首，全诗完整。第二句“乐樵苏”，《万首唐人绝句》作“乐樵渔”；题目一些古本误作“已亥岁”。

lines.py: zé guó jiāng shān rù zhàn tú
lines.lit: The rivers and hills of the marshland have entered the war maps;
lines.en: Even the lakes and hills of the south are on the war maps now;

lines.py: shēng mín hé jì lè qiáo sū
lines.lit: by what means can the people enjoy gathering firewood and grass?
lines.en: how can common folk still go out for firewood in peace?

lines.py: píng jūn mò huà fēng hóu shì
lines.lit: I ask you, sir, do not speak of being made a lord;
lines.en: Please don’t talk to me of earning titles and glory —

lines.py: yī jiàng gōng chéng wàn gǔ kū
lines.lit: one general’s merit is achieved; ten thousand bones wither.
lines.en: for one general’s triumph, ten thousand men lie bleached to bone.

words.en: Jihai, a year in the sixty-year cycle (here 879)
words.note: 干支纪年，今天农历仍用，如“甲辰年”。

words.en: land of lakes and marshes; the water country of the south
words.note: 书面语，今天形容洪水时还说“一片泽国”。
今天也常用，也指国家政权，如“打江山”。
“樵”是砍柴，今天还有“樵夫”；“苏”这个意思今天不用了。
古义“请您”，今天“凭”多指“依靠”。

words.en: to be made a marquis — to win high rank
words.note: 泛指建立功业、得到高官。

words.py: yī jiàng gōng chéng wàn gǔ kū
words.en: one general’s success costs ten thousand lives
words.note: 今天仍常引用，批评战争或靠别人牺牲换来的个人功名。

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 江南水乡本来是安宁富饶的地方，如今江河湖泊都成了战场，美好和残酷形成对比。
imagery.en: The rivers of the south once meant peace and plenty; now they are battle lines, and the contrast makes the war feel even crueller.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: “江山入战图”，山河都被画进作战地图，写出战火遍地、无处可逃。
imagery.en: The hills and rivers drawn onto war maps show that fighting has spread everywhere, leaving nowhere to hide.
